claims.text: Introducing nanoscale Y2O3 particles into a refractory high-entropy alloy will produce an oxide-dispersion-strengthened microstructure.
Nanoscale oxide particles will impede dislocation motion in the alloy matrix.
Nanoscale oxide particles will interact with irradiation-induced defects.
The oxide dispersions will produce Orowan strengthening by obstructing dislocation glide.
The oxide dispersions may absorb irradiation-generated defects or mitigate their clustering.
Reduced clustering of irradiation-generated defects will reduce embrittlement.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will have higher yield strength than the otherwise comparable alloy without oxide dispersions.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will have greater resistance to irradiation-induced degradation than the alloy without oxide dispersions.
Adding nanoscale Y2O3 dispersions will not compromise the alloy's high-temperature thermal stability.
The predicted benefits are intended to hold during prolonged exposure at temperatures of at least approximately 1000 degrees Celsius and under significant neutron or ion irradiation.
Significant coarsening of the oxide particles under thermal or irradiation exposure may eliminate the predicted mechanical benefits.
Poor interfacial bonding between the oxide particles and alloy matrix may degrade the predicted mechanical improvements.
Long-term retention of nanoscale particle size and effective dispersion under simultaneous high-temperature and irradiation exposure is uncertain.
The evolution of oxide–matrix interfaces during long-term high-temperature and irradiation exposure is uncertain.
